name: The 11th Angkor Empire Marathon 2026
short_description: A 42.195 km full marathon held in front of Angkor Wat Temple, Siem Reap, Cambodia, on August 2, 2026.
ai_summary: The 11th Angkor Empire Marathon 2026 is a full marathon covering 42.195 km, scheduled for August 2, 2026, in front of Angkor Wat Temple in Siem Reap, Cambodia. This edition marks the eleventh running of the event at this historic location. Registration for the race has not yet been announced, so prospective runners should check back for updates on how to sign up.

core_facts.venue: In front of Angkor Wat Temple, Siem Reap

pros: Iconic setting in front of Angkor Wat Temple, a landmark venue in Siem Reap
Standard full-marathon distance of 42.195 km for a well-established race format
Long-running event now in its 11th edition, indicating an established history
cons: Registration status is not yet announced, so entry details are currently unavailable

excerpt_quotes.quote: This is a small marathon run through Siem Reap and Ankor Wat. The course is flat and easy but the humidity ate me up along with a 4am arrival to start at 4:30 am. The start was really dark for the first few miles..
Not many spectators but the local kids will break your heart as they are so excited to see the runners and try to run with you for a short distance..
The scenic route of the Angkor Empire Marathon is proving a big drawcard for serious runners and tourists from far and wide
excerpt_quotes.attribution: South China Morning Post feature on Cambodia's Angkor marathons

research_highlights: Course is flat and mostly paved, running through Angkor Archaeological Park past nearly 40 ancient temples including Bayon and the South Gate of Angkor Thom
Race starts at 4:30 AM in front of Angkor Wat, so the first stretch of the course is run in darkness
August timing means heat and especially humidity are a major factor; the 2025 edition drew over 4,000 runners from 51 countries and 2026 organisers expect around 4,500
Four distance options (3km, 10km, half marathon, marathon), with the full and half marathon AIMS-recognised/certified courses
Local children along the route are reported as an enthusiastic, memorable part of the atmosphere even where formal spectator crowds are thin
research_watchouts: Humidity is repeatedly flagged by runners as the toughest element of the race, even though the course itself is flat and easy
Very early 4:30 AM start means a pre-3 AM wake-up and a dark first few kilometres with limited visibility
Outside the main Angkor Wat start/finish area, spectator support along the course is reportedly sparse
Runners caution against booking temple tours or heavy sightseeing for the afternoon immediately after the race due to fatigue
